name: Penis enlargement surgery

lead: Penis enlargement surgery includes ligament release, fat grafting and filler or silicone injection to increase length or girth.
Urology societies say the evidence is limited and low quality, and surgery is not medically indicated except for micropenis.

paras: Procedures either release ligament attachments to expose more length, or add volume with fat, filler or grafts.
Reported harms include scarring, shortening, deformity, infection, necrosis and erectile dysfunction. Fillers are not FDA-approved for this use.

lead: Penis enlargement surgery covers surgical and injectable procedures meant to increase penile length or girth, including suspensory ligament release, fat injection or grafting, dermal fillers and silicone or PMMA injection [1][2]. Wikipedia states it is not medically indicated except for micropenis [1].

Professional bodies are cautious. The American Urological Association says fat injection for girth and ligament division for length have not been shown safe or efficacious, and the Sexual Medicine Society of North America issued a 2024 position statement on cosmetic penile enhancement that advises against permanent fillers [1][3]. A 2024 systematic review examined outcomes, complications and quality of life after penile augmentation [4]. In looksmaxxing culture the topic is grouped under hardmaxxing.
infobox: Ligament release, fat grafting, fillers, implants
Position statement; advises against permanent fillers [1][3]

paras: Suspensory ligament release increases flaccid length but not erect length and can affect sexual function [1]. Fat transfer can enlarge girth but the gain may fade, and fat injection can cause swelling and deformity [1]. Injectable fillers including hyaluronic acid have shown limited efficacy, while dermal fillers are not FDA-approved for this use [1]. An Italian series from 1995 to 1997 described an albugineal surgery with saphenous vein grafts in 39 patients seeking more girth [5].

A 2008 review noted that long-term data and patient-rated satisfaction were lacking in many studies [6]. A 2019 review summarised by Wikipedia described outcomes as poor, with low satisfaction and evidence that is scant and low quality [1].

Reported complications include scarring that may lead to shortening or erectile dysfunction, deformity, infection and necrosis. Liquid silicone injection in Vietnam in 2013 led to hospitalisations for infections, necrosis, tumors and sexual dysfunction [1]. A 1997 Journal of Urology paper described reconstruction of deformities resulting from enlargement surgery [7].

Studies are mostly surgical case series and reviews. A 2024 systematic review summarised outcomes and complications of penile augmentation techniques [4], and the SMSNA position statement gave recommendations for injection and surgical procedures and for future research [3]. A registered trial is examining penile lengthening before penile prosthesis implantation in men with erectile dysfunction [8].

timeline.event: AUA first publishes position that fat injection and ligament division are not shown safe or effective [1].
SMSNA position statement and systematic review published [3][4].
